memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'So then, it was not you who sent me here, but God. He made me father to Pharaoh, lord of his entire household and ruler of all Egypt.'" — Gen 45:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"It was not you who sent me here, but God." Joseph is not denying the facts — he has already said plainly, "you sold me." He is telling them where the ultimate hand lies. Behind the jealousy of ten brothers and the greed of a caravan of traders, God was directing the whole thing towards a purpose none of them could see.

And look at the titles Joseph now carries: father to Pharaoh, lord of his household, ruler of all Egypt. This is the boy they threw in a pit because they could not stand his dreams. God did not merely rescue him; He raised him. The path went down before it went up — Potiphar's house, then prison, then the palace — but every step downward was part of the way up.

That is a pattern Scripture returns to again and again. The One who humbled Himself to death on a cross was exalted to the highest place, and given a name above every name (Phil 2:8-9). Humiliation before exaltation. Suffering before glory.

If God has you in a low place today, it does not mean He has forgotten you or that His plans have failed. Joseph's pit was not a detour from the palace. It was the road to it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you interpret a low season — as failure, or as part of God's road?
2. Where have you seen God's hand behind circumstances you could not control?
3. What does Christ's own path of humility before glory teach you about your own?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I cannot see Your hand, help me trust Your heart. Thank You that low places are not the end of Your story for me, just as the cross was not the end of Yours. Amen.
